The '''1998–99 Scottish Premier League''' season (also known as the '''1998–99 [[Bank of Scotland]] Scottish Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons from 11 March<ref name="Scottish sponsorship deal is defended">{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4971530.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019151242/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-4971530.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=2012-10-19|work=[[The Independent]]|title=Scottish sponsorship deal is defended|date=1999-03-11|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|access-date=2008-04-21}}</ref>) was the inaugural season of [[Scottish Premier League]] football, the top division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish]] [[Association football|football]]. It began on 1 August 1998 and concluded on 23 May 1999.

The league was made up of the ten clubs that broke away from the [[Scottish Football League]] at the end of the [[1997–98 in Scottish football|1997–98 season]]. [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] went into the season as the defending Scottish champions, having won the [[1997–98 Scottish Premier Division]].

[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] won the title with 3 matches still to play on 2 May 1999, after defeating [[Old Firm]] rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] 3–0 in controversial circumstances at [[Celtic Park]].<ref name="Celtic 0-3 Rangers">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/scottish_premier/334094.stm|work=[[BBC News]]|title=Rangers make history out of chaos |date=1999-05-03|access-date=2008-04-20}}</ref> Three players were red-carded during the game and referee [[Hugh Dallas]] was struck by a coin thrown by a Celtic supporter and required treatment from paramedics on the field.<ref name="Celtic 0-3 Rangers"/>

==Teams==
On 8 September 1997, the clubs in the [[Scottish Football League Premier Division|Premier Division]] decided to split from the [[Scottish Football League]] and form a [[Scottish Premier League]] (SPL). This followed [[Premier League#Foundation (1990s)|an earlier example in England]], which came into force during the [[1992–93 in English football|1992–93 season]]. This decision was fuelled by a desire by the top clubs in Scotland to retain more of the revenue generated by the game. Originally, league sponsorship money was divided proportionally between clubs in all four divisions. After the SPL was formed, its clubs retained all of its commercial revenues except for an annual payment to the SFL and a parachute payment to relegated clubs.

The new league followed the same format as the previous season's Premier Division, with the ten clubs playing each other four times, twice at home and twice away. [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] were relegated to the [[1998–99 Scottish First Division|First Division]] after finishing bottom of the [[1997–98 Scottish Premier Division]]. They were replaced by [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], the champions of the [[1997–98 Scottish First Division|previous season's First Division]].

==Overview==
The 1998–99 Scottish Premier League season ended in success for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who, managed by Dutchman [[Dick Advocaat]], won the title by six points from nearest rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] were relegated after three seasons in the top division. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Celtic were joined by [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Fourth placed [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] also gained a UEFA Cup place via the [[UEFA Fair Play ranking]].[[Image:Kanchelskis Andrei.jpg|thumb|right|130px|The £5.5m transfer of [[Andrei Kanchelskis]] to Rangers set a new Scottish transfer record.]]

The season began on 1 August 1998 with the first SPL goal scored by [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]'s [[Eoin Jess]] as they defeated newly promoted [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] 2–0 at [[Dens Park]].<ref name="Season review">{{cite news|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/season-review-199899-2008-06-01/|publisher=spfl.co.uk|title=Season Review - 1998-1999|access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref> Also on the first day of the season, [[Craig Burley]] scored the SPL's first [[hat-trick]] as defending champions Celtic defeated Dunfermline Athletic  5–0 at [[Celtic Park]].<ref name="Season review"/>

1998–99 saw the introduction of a three-week break during January, which was well received by both players and managers.<ref name="Season review"/> In its inaugural year, the SPL was broadcast to over 120 countries worldwide,<ref name="Season review"/> while attendances increased<ref name="Season review"/> and more money was invested in youth development than ever before.<ref name="Season review"/> A new Scottish transfer record was also set as Rangers paid [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] £5.5m for former [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] [[winger (football)|winger]] [[Andrei Kanchelskis]].<ref name="Kanchelskis move to Rangers ">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/133326.stm|work=[[BBC News]]|title=Kanchelskis move to Rangers|date=1998-07-15|access-date=2008-04-20}}</ref>

Rangers clinched the SPL title on 2 May 1999 by beating [[Old Firm]]-rivals Celtic 3–0 at [[Celtic Park]].<ref name="Celtic 0-3 Rangers"/> Three players were red-carded during the game and referee [[Hugh Dallas]] was struck by a coin thrown by a Celtic supporter and required treatment from paramedics on the field.<ref name="Celtic 0-3 Rangers"/>

Dunfermline Athletic were relegated to the [[Scottish First Division]] on 8 May 1999 after a 2–1 defeat to Celtic at [[East End Park]].<ref name="Dunfermline 1–2 Celtic">{{cite news|url=http://www.thecelticwiki.com/page/1999-05-08%3A+Dunfermline+1-2+Celtic%2C+Premier+League|publisher=The Celtic Wiki|title=1999-05-08: Dunfermline 1-2 Celtic, Premier League|access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref>
